input.quote: 28.1 This Agreement is governed exclusively by Singapore law, and the courts of Singapore have exclusive jurisdiction.
input.rationale: Section 28.1 selects Singapore law and exclusive Singapore jurisdiction, which is outside the accepted list (New York, Delaware, California, England and Wales) and is Vendor-favourable walk-away territory; it also directly conflicts with Section 28.2, which already grants exclusive jurisdiction to the state and federal courts in New York County with only a customary temporary injunctive relief carve-out (that carve-out does not defeat an otherwise exclusive merits forum). The shortest complete cure is to change the governing law in 28.1 to New York and delete the conflicting Singapore forum, leaving 28.2 as the sole venue; the preferred forum element is therefore already met verbatim.

mappings.element: New York law governs the Agreement.
State and federal courts in New York County have exclusive jurisdiction over the merits, subject only to temporary injunctive relief elsewhere.
mappings.quote: The state and federal courts located in New York County, New York have exclusive jurisdiction, and each Party irrevocably submits to personal jurisdiction and waives any objection based on venue or inconvenient forum. Nothing prevents a Party from seeking temporary injunctive relief in another court with jurisdiction to protect confidential information or intellectual property.

proposal.summary: Replace Singapore governing law and Singapore exclusive jurisdiction with New York law, leaving 28.2's New York County forum as the sole venue.
proposal.comment: [Playbook] We have moved governing law to New York, which is our preferred position, and removed the Singapore forum because it directly conflicts with Section 28.2's exclusive New York County jurisdiction. Delaware, California, or England and Wales law with the corresponding courts would be an acceptable fallback.
